problem:
Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-1,\,y=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+2$
from $t=0$ to $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ ?

feedback.problem:
Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$
from $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ to $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ ?
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t))=3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))^{2}+(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t))^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+9{cos}^{2}⁡(3t)}\,\text{d}t\,.\end{aligned}
$$
